question: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours, but with a leak it takes 40 hours. The leak lets out 14 litres a minute. What is the capacity of the tank?
solution: The pipe fills 1/15 of it an hour; with the leak only 1/40 stays, so the leak takes out 1/15 − 1/40 an hour and empties it alone in 15 × 40 ÷ (40 − 15) = 24 hours = 1440 minutes. At 14 litres a minute that is 1440 × 14 = 20160 litres.

question: Pipe A can fill a water tank in 3 hours. Pipe B lets out 16 litres a minute. With both open, the tank fills in 7 hours. What is its capacity?
solution: In an hour A puts in C/3 and B takes out 16 × 60 = 960 litres; together C/7. So C/3 − C/7 = 960, i.e. C × 4/21 = 960 and C = 960 × 21 ÷ 4 = 5040 litres.

question: Pipes A and B can fill a water tank in 10 and 15 hours, and pipe C can empty it in 8 hours. A and B are opened on an empty tank, and C is opened 3 hours later. In how many hours from the start will it be full?
solution: The tank = LCM(10, 15, 8) = 120 units. First 3 hours: 3 × 20 = 60. Then 20 − 15 = 5 an hour for the remaining 60: 12 hours. Total 3 + 12 = 15 hours.

question: Pipe P can fill a tank in 44 minutes and pipe Q can empty it in 132 minutes. If both are opened when the tank is empty, in how many minutes will it be full?
solution: The tank = LCM(44, 132) = 132 units. P fills 3, Q empties 1: net 2 a minute. Time = 132 ÷ 2 = 66 minutes.

question: Three pipes X, Y and Z can fill a cistern in 4, 10 and 20 hours respectively. X is opened at 7:00 AM, Y at 8:00 AM and Z at 9:00 AM. At what time will the cistern be full?
solution: The cistern = LCM(4, 10, 20) = 20 units. 7:00 AM–8:00 AM: X alone, 5. 8:00 AM–9:00 AM: X and Y, 7. Filled 12, left 8; all three fill 8 an hour: 1 hours more. Full at 10:00 AM.

question: Pipes A and B can fill a water tank in 15 and 36 hours respectively. Both are opened together, but A is closed 2 hours before the tank is full. In how many hours is it full?
